# vendor

Running GE's own `pet_recon` on this machine.

The objective is to obtain **randoms, scatter, normalisation and dead time**
from the vendor binary rather than reimplementing them in Python.

All four are obtainable. Section 3 is the status table, section 3a gives the
correct call sequence, section 3b covers norm × dead time, section 3c covers
randoms and scatter, and section 3d covers supplying a locally computed mu-map
to the single-scatter simulation.

---

## 0. Packaging

The docker image `d710:full` contains GE's vendor tree. Beyond that, `run.sh`
mounts exactly two things: this directory (`/vendor`, read-only) and the output
directory (`/out`, writable).

```
extract.gdb   the main procedure
 ├─ boot.gdb  brings pet_recon to idle; publishes 3 AP globals; clears DF; locks
 ├─ lib.gdb   python helpers: say/ex/show/setv/deep/dump_views/unlocked/clear_df
 └─ job.gdb   loads a .job into IgJobReq (524 fields); generated by job2gdb.py
```

Those four files must sit together in `/vendor`. The remainder runs on the host
and does not enter the container:

```
estimate.py    the entry point: raw data plus CT to all four sinograms, in one command
run.sh         runs one gdb script in the container (invoked by estimate.py)
Dockerfile     builds d710:full — pet_recon plus custom_tool, self-contained
job2gdb.py     .job to job.gdb
read_out.py    reads out/*.f32 together with the .json sidecar
make_pifa.py   builds and decodes a PIFA, the mu-map container
ct_to_pifa.py  CT DICOM to mu in mm^-1 to PIFA, for a real case
```

`probes/` is scaffolding. It is not needed to run the tool and is kept as
evidence for the conclusions in this document; see `probes/README.md`.

### Running

```bash
docker load -i d710_full.tar
export D710_OUT=~/UET/d710_out

d710 estimate --raw <the exam's petRDFS directory> \
              --ct  <the CT DICOM series directory> \
              --case <case name>
```

Add `--bed 4` for a single bed. Output is written to
`$D710_OUT/<case>/vendor/bed<n>/`.

There is no `--norm` requirement: the exam declares its own norm file and the
tool resolves it (section 0b). The flag exists only to force a different file.

`estimate.py` performs the whole sequence: it reads the bed's table position
from the RDF header, builds a mu-map from the CT on the PIFA grid, generates the
job, and runs `pet_recon` in the container with the data mounted read-only and
`--out` mounted directly at `/out`, so that the kernel writes its results in
place.

It runs under a bare `python3`: no conda, no numpy and no pydicom. Every step
that needs a library runs inside the image (`ct_to_pifa.py`, and reading the
calibration DICOM), and every vendor file it reads is likewise in the image. It
remains on the host only because it is the component that *invokes* `docker`.
`tests/test_estimate.py` fixes that property by scanning this file's imports.

A verified example on NEMA bed 2, with real data:

```
prompts 13,954,115  ==  RDF header      -> the expected data
randoms/prompts            12.3 %
scatter fraction S/(T+S)   33.0 %
radial roughness: scatter 0.071  against  prompts 1.747
```

If resolution fails and no `--norm` is given, the tool falls back to GE's norm
self-test and warns prominently: randoms and scatter are unaffected, but
`normdt.f32` and `norm_only.f32` are then the sensitivity of GE's test machine
rather than of this one.

> List mode is not accepted directly. A `LIST*.BLF` must first be histogrammed
> into a `SINO*` (`d710 decode --listmode`). Every `LIST*.BLF` on disk has a
> `SINO*` from the same acquisition; supply that file.

Running the steps by hand remains possible:
`./run.sh --out <directory> extract.gdb` uses the default `job.gdb`. `--out` is
required and has no default. It was formerly a fixed `vendor/out/`, which meant
every run passed through one shared directory: two beds running concurrently
overwrote each other's results, and 7.5 GB of output accumulated inside the
source tree.

---

## 0b. `--norm`: whether this machine has a norm file, and how that is known

It does, and exactly one, which is not a coincidence: the export carries the
calibration scan the exam references, because the exam declares it in its own
header.

RDF header offset `0xEEC` is `norm_cal_uid`; `ge_rdf_tool.py info` still
mislabels it `study_instance_uid`, and `0xF74 = wcc_cal_uid` is likewise
mislabelled `series_instance_uid`. The full chain is verifiable at every step,
and `estimate.py` follows it automatically, which is why `--norm` is
unnecessary:

```
NEMA SINO0001  header 0xEEC = 1.2.840.113619.2.290.663120.1697775916.195435
   -> cal/1.2.840...195435.3dnorm         (508 B DICOM, purely bookkeeping;
        (0017,1005) PET 3D Normalization   it contains no coefficients)
        (0017,1007) /petRDFS/JFEJGPAB/SYSNDZAQ/PQRPXCCJ/SINO0001
        (0017,1004) 20231020112516.00
   -> 12082026/petRDFS/JFEJGPAB/SYSNDZAQ/PQRPXCCJ/SINO0001   present
```

The match is on the absolute path, so there is no room for ambiguity. A copy is
kept in the repository under `cal/`, so the tool still runs when an export
arrives without its calibration. For the contents of the norm file and the
two-scanner table on the console, see `cal/README.md`.

### The calibration register holds seven entries, and WCC is not 3D norm

| date | type | source scan | present on disk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022-12-29 | 3DWCC Annulus | `/petRDFS/HBJMGPAB/...` | no |
| 2023-10-20 | PET 3D Normalization | `/petRDFS/JFEJGPAB/SYSNDZAQ/PQRPXCCJ/SINO0001` | yes |
| 2024-06-07 | PET 3D Normalization | `/petRDFS/NQNGGPAB/SYUKRVRX/ZVOAMELQ/SINO0001` | no |
| 2025-02-21 | PET 3D Normalization | `/petRDFS/NQPDZCAC/.../SINO0002` | no |
| 2025-02-21 | PET 3D Normalization | `/petRDFS/NQPDZCAC/.../SINO0003` | no |
| 2025-02-24 | PET 3D Normalization | `/petRDFS/NQNGGPAB/SYEWRVTO/FRLMEOTO/SINO0001` | no |
| 2025-02-24 | PET 3D Normalization | `/petRDFS/NQNGGPAB/MNICTYEA/RNHFDCKE/SINO0001` | no |

The well-counter calibration and the 3D normalisation are distinct; GE labels
them separately at `(0017,1005)`. The actual 3DWCC Annulus scan lies under
`HBJMGPAB/...` and is not present in the export.

### The 2026 exams still reference the 2023-10-20 calibration

The machine was recalibrated on 2024-06-07, twice on 2025-02-21 and twice on
2025-02-24 for station DXRM3, yet all three 2026 exams declare the
`norm_cal_uid` and `wcc_cal_uid` of 2023-10-20. This is not inferred from the
header alone: the console keeps a register of the active calibration in
`systemConfig/cal/.default`, which states it directly:

```
3dgeom | 1.2.840.113619.2.131.1459872910.1219799569.748327
3dnorm | 1.2.840.113619.2.290.663120.1697775916.195435     <- 2023-10-20
3dwcc  | 1.2.840.113619.2.290.663120.1697776129.151600     <- 2023-10-20
```

That file was last modified on 2026-07-17, eleven days before the paediatric
case, and `.default.old` (2026-03-11) records the same values. All three UID
fields of the RDF header match these lines character for character, including
the field `ge_rdf_tool` calls `device_uid`, which is in fact the UID of the
`3dgeom` calibration — a third mislabelled field of the same kind as 0xEEC and
0xF74.

A further confirmation of this reading of 0xEEC: the 2023-10-20 norm scan itself
declares its own 0xEEC as `...1692003848...`, that is 2023-08-14, the
calibration active when *it* was acquired.

The calibration in use is therefore about 2.8 years old, outside every published
recommendation (GE: quarterly; ACR, IAEA and EANM: at least annually). There are
signs that later calibrations were run but not committed: 2025-02-24 carries
three WCC files about ten minutes apart (12:12:56, 12:18:45, 12:32:38) with the
same Activity Factor of 4.008868, which is the pattern of repeated attempts. On
a GE console a WCC or norm acquisition must be accepted and installed before it
replaces the previous one, and `.default` is where that is recorded.

The effect on this work is small: the Activity Factor drifts 4.0628 → 3.9854 →
4.0089, roughly ±1 %, and `K` is measured independently, so GE's absolute scale
does not enter the result directly. The greater concern is detector uniformity
after 2.8 years rather than the overall factor.

### The norm file is loaded, and it takes effect

`CNorm3d::Initialize()` returns `GRE_IG_SUCCESS`, and the result differs
measurably from the norm self-test:

```
norm self-test   :  normdt  0.134 … 4.478   mean 1.011
this machine's   :  normdt  0.466 … 3.280   mean 1.029   <- tighter, more norm-like
```

> That demonstrates the file is loaded and effective. It does not demonstrate
> that every coefficient is interpreted correctly: `Initialize()` may return
> SUCCESS on data it misreads. Confirmation requires NEMA — a correct norm must
> flatten a uniform phantom, and the current axial deviation is about ±15 %.

### Results

Each `.f32` is accompanied by a `.json` recording shape, statistics and
provenance, in `out/`:

| file | content | dtype and shape |
|---|---|---|
| `randoms.f32` | randoms | f32, 288 × 553 × 381 |
| `scatter.f32` | SSS scatter | f32, 288 × 553 × 381 |
| `normdt.f32` | norm × dead time, a sensitivity | f32, 288 × 553 × 381 |
| `norm_only.f32` | norm alone, so that `dead time = normdt / norm_only` | f32, 288 × 553 × 381 |
| `prompts.u16` | the emission sinogram as loaded | u16, 288 × 553 × 381 |
| `singles.i32` | per-crystal singles | i32, 576 × 24 |
| `dt_int.f32`, `dt_mux.f32` | dead time per block | f32, 256 |
| `estimate.json` | provenance: input paths, table position, RDF header | JSON |

No well-counter calibration is applied anywhere, which leaves the absolute scale
free for independent calibration.

### Changing the input data by hand

`estimate.py` generates `job.gdb` from a genuine GE XR job and replaces only
three paths; the remaining 521 fields are GE's. To do this manually:

```bash
./job2gdb.py <file.job> /out/ovl > job.gdb
```

or edit three lines in `job.gdb` directly: `inputEmissionFileName[0]` for the
emission sinogram, `normalizationSinogramFile` for the norm, and
`inputTransmissionFileName[0]` for the PIFA mu-map.

`extract.gdb` reads the job from the environment variable `D710_JOB`, defaulting
to `/vendor/job.gdb`, and `run.sh` additionally mounts `D710_DATA` at `/data`,
which is how `estimate.py` supplies data from outside the image.

A PIFA for a real case — the disk holds only four self-test files and none for
any of these exams — is built by `ct_to_pifa.py`, which `estimate.py` invokes.
To call it separately:

```bash
python ct_to_pifa.py <CT dir> out/mu.pifa --table-location -125.17
python make_pifa.py --inspect out/mu.pifa
```

`ct_to_pifa.py` takes the `FrameOfReferenceUID` of the CT series itself by
default, which is what `ValidateCTAC` requires (section 3d), so this is normally
not a consideration.

## 1. What has been unlocked

`pet_recon` requires ten 64-bit shared objects. All ten are present, in two
locations:

```
petsw/usr/g/PET/lib64/linux2/    libpetcfg libconfigMgr librdf libErr libpetlwc
                                 (+ libOpenCL.so.1)   <- /usr/PET/lib64 points here
petsw/usr/lib64/                 libreadcfg libeventmgr libmsghand libcupipc
                                 libstartup.so.1
```

`ldd` inside the namespace reports no missing libraries. `pet_recon` starts,
reads `coremap.cfg.parc3` and creates six processing threads.

### A GPU is not required for the four quantities sought

Established with `nm`: every `Ocl*` class in the binary takes
`OsemTofGpu::COsemTofValues` — `OclFwdProj`, `OclBackProj`, `OclRatioStep`,
`OclImageUpdate`, `OclPsfAxial`, `OclPsfRadial` and `OclScatUpsample`. The GPU
therefore runs OSEM, not the corrections. Randoms, scatter, norm and dead time
are all `sharcAp*` kernels on the CPU.

Disabling the GPU therefore costs nothing here. It is also not optional: the
machine has no OpenCL platform, and GE did not ship the kernel sources —
`find petsw -name '*.cl'` returns no files, because they reside on the chassis
accelerator at 10.1.1.x.

---

## 2. The image

Section 0 covers how to run it; this section explains its construction.

`d710:full` contains `/usr/PET`, `/usr/g` and `/vendorlib` directly, so `petsw/`
is no longer mounted. Only two small mounts remain: `/vendor` (this directory,
read-only, so that gdb scripts can be edited without a rebuild) and `/out`.

`./run.sh --mount ...` is a fallback that uses the base stage: it binds `petsw/`
from the host, and then requires a writable copy of `systemConfig` (about
1.4 GB), which `run.sh` creates under `--cache` (default `$D710_OUT/.cache`) so
that it survives between beds. `d710:full` exists precisely to avoid this.

### `COPY` rather than `docker commit`

This was formerly done by a `bake.sh` script: bind-mount `petsw/` into a
temporary container, copy inside it, then `docker commit`. The reason was the
build context, since `COPY` makes docker send all 18 GB to the daemon.

An image produced by `commit` is perfectly pushable and pullable — it is an
ordinary image, and the `-v` mounts exist only during the copy and do not
reference the build machine afterwards. The problem is that nobody can rebuild
it: the Dockerfile does not describe its contents, so the recipient has
something that runs but cannot be modified.

A `.dockerignore` at the project root addresses the context problem at its
source, so the copy is now a genuine `COPY`. It is also where the unnecessary
material is excluded; most of those 18 GB are never touched by `pet_recon`:

| excluded | size |
|---|---:|
| `usr/g/service/log/pet_iow_service.log` | 9.2 GB |
| `usr/g/service/matlab/library{32,64}` | ~450 MB |
| `usr/g/service/tools/.../vct_helical.ffp` | 233 MB |
| `usr/g/service/dicomtools` | |

Also excluded are `usr/lib` (842 MB of the console's 32-bit libraries; the ones
actually loaded are in `usr/PET/lib/linux2`) and 1.1 GB of `usr/lib64` except
for five files. What remains is `usr/PET` at 1.8 GB and `usr/g` at 1.8 GB,
giving a context of about 3.6 GB and an image of 7.3 GB, which includes the i386
toolchain and numpy, scipy, pydicom and petsird for the decode side.
`service/log/` is recreated empty because `pet_recon` writes `IG1.timers.log`
into it.

> The 9.2 GB log file is a console service log rather than data. It can be
> deleted to reclaim space, but it lies within the vendor tree, so
> `.dockerignore` only excludes it from the context and does not modify the
> original.

### Test data, on the correct model, with reference results

```
/usr/PET/release/petig/selftest/          (already inside the image)
  test_protocols_kh/XR/selftest_kh_3dir.job     a genuine XR job, that is, D710
  data/selftest_kh3d_ex.rdf                     emission
  data/selftest_kh3d_norm.rdf                   norm
  data/selftest_kh3d_pifa.dat                   PIFA (the mu-map for scatter)
  gold_standard/job1.0 … job1.N                 reference images for comparison
```

| step | status |

| `sharcCmpOpenDataFiles(&IgJobReq)` | complete, returns 0 |
| `apCfg` and `sysGeometry` populated from the RDF header | complete |
| self-contained docker image `d710:full`, boots correctly | complete |
| dump the whole of `apCfg` and `sysGeometry` at run time | complete; see `PARAMS.md` |
| `InitParamStruct` to live geometry (381 × 553 × 288, 55 TOF) | complete |
| `Deallocate` then `ReallocateBuffs` allocating 1 GB | complete |
| `CIgManager::LoadRawData()` | complete, GRE_IG_SUCCESS |
| load singles (`sharcCmp3dRemoteSinglesLoad`) | complete |
| load dead time (`sharcCmp3dRemoteDeadtimeLoad`) | complete |
| load norm (`setup3dEmissJob(jobReq, false)`) | complete |

| locally computed mu-map injected into `m_pAttn` for SSS | complete; sections 3c and 3d |
| attenuation sinogram through `CCTAC_3D` | not done — `DoTask` segfaults, and it is unnecessary: attenuation is rebuilt by `utils/attenuation.py` |
| `sharcCmpProcessJobOnAp(...)` running to completion | not done — deadlocks; section 3a replaces it |

## 3a. The correct call sequence, taken from `CIgManager::RunCyclic`

`RunCyclic` is the coordinating function, and the order in which it calls is the
order that is required:

```
CleanDataBuffers(false)
InitParamStruct()                 <- fills GRE_IG_PARAMETER_STRUCT from apCfg/RDF
CRawDataMem::DeallocateBuffs(false, ig)
CCorrDataMem::DeallocateBuffs(false, ig)
CRawDataMem::ReallocateBuffs(false, ig)
CCorrDataMem::ReallocateBuffs(false, ig)
CImageDataMem::ReallocateBuffs(false, ig)
LoadRawData()                     <- CRawDataLoad on the thread pool
DoProcessing()                    <- InitLuts, InitRandomsFromSingles, ...
```

Calling `Deallocate` before `Reallocate` is not a formality. `ReallocateBuffs`
begins with `if (GetNumAllocViews() != 0) skip`, and a freshly constructed
`CViewBuffer` already reports one element of two bytes. Without the
`Deallocate`, every `Reallocate` returns `GRE_IG_SUCCESS` while allocating
nothing, and `CRawDataLoad` can place only view 0 before reporting
`can't reserve view 1` (RawDataLoad.cpp:154). That is the sole cause of the
`LoadRawData` failure; it is not the `bool` argument of `ReallocateBuffs`, which
`RunCyclic` always passes as `false`.

After correct allocation:

```
RawPrompts   288 views × 421386 B  = 121 MB   (2 B × 381 × 553)
RawDelays    288 views × 421386 B
RawNorm       47 views × 647168 B
CorrPrompts  288 views × 842772 B  = 242 MB   (4 B × 381 × 553)
CorrRandoms  288 views × 842772 B
CorrScatter  288 views × 842772 B
```

### Three globals that `CPCCommThread` must publish

`boot.gdb` terminates `CPCCommThread` at entry because it calls
`opendir("/petRDFS/OVLFILES")` and then `exit(-1)`. However, its first three
statements (cpcMain.cpp:234-236) are not socket work: they publish three globals
that every `sharcCmp*` and `sharcAp*` kernel dereferences.

```
m_pRawDataMem   = arg[0]   @ 0xf38948
m_pImageDataMem = arg[1]   @ 0xf38950
m_pParamStruct  = arg[2]   @ 0xf38958
```

Omitting those three assignments is the cause of the `LoadRawData()` SIGSEGV at
`0x516da5` inside `sharcCmp3dRemoteLoadPrompts`, which executes
`mov m_pRawDataMem,%rax ; mov (%rax),%r14` on a null global. The member
`CIgManager::m_pRawDataMem` remains valid throughout, because the AP side never
consults that member. `boot.gdb` now replays the three stores before returning.

### Loading singles, dead time and norm: three separate AP paths

`LoadRawData` loads prompts only. The other three have their own entry points,
and all are on the AP side and therefore require no FIFO:

| quantity | call | condition |
|---|---|---|
| singles | `sharcCmp3dRemoteSinglesLoad(&IgJobReq, 0xf38968)` | `emissionRandomsFlag == 3`, `singlesType == 0` |
| dead time | `sharcCmp3dRemoteDeadtimeLoad(&IgJobReq, 0xf38980)` | `(1 << deadtimeType) & 0xd` |
| norm and attenuation | `setup3dEmissJob(&IgJobReq, false)` | `normalizationFlag`, `attenuationFlag` |

`setup3dEmissJob` with its `bool` parameter false skips the emission segment
loading loop, which `LoadRawData` has already performed, and loads only norm and
attenuation.

The two structures `loadSinglesStruct` and `loadDeadtimeStruct` are file-scope
globals of anonymous type in DWARF, so gdb cannot name their fields; they are
written through fixed addresses, the binary being non-PIE. Both have the layout
`{s32 status; s32 dragonSocketStatus; n32 type;}`.

---

## 3b. Norm × dead time

`out/normdt.f32` is 288 × 553 × 381 float32, 231.5 MB, with no zero entries,
min 0.1229, max 4.0872, mean 0.9246, and a view-to-view spread of only 4.5 %.

The formula is GE's, taken from `CAccelIntfNormDTData::ApplyNormDeadtime`
(0x4a39e0), the function that builds the NormDT sinogram for the accelerator,
and reproduced identically by `COsem3dPrep::DoPrep`:

```c
GE_vfill(1.0f, work, number_v_theta * numberSamples);        // one view of all 1.0
if (IgJobReq.normalizationFlag)
    CNorm3d::ApplyNormalization(work, phi, scratch, false);
if (IgJobReq.emissionDeadTimeFlag)
    CDeadtime3d::ApplyDeadtime(work, phi, work, 0, &f1, &f2, scratch, false);
// then PadData / projTranspose / p_rev4, which is packaging for the
// accelerator and is deliberately not reproduced by extract.gdb
```

Feeding the kernel a sinogram of all ones is what turns the result into
*correction factors* rather than *corrected data*.

`scratch` must be five times one view; `NewReconRequest` allocates exactly
`5 * numberSamples * number_v_theta` floats.

### No well-counter calibration is included

`ApplyNormalization` and `ApplyDeadtime` do not touch `wccActivityFactor`,
`wccSensitivityFactor` or `m_fwccScaleFactor`, and `extract.gdb` calls nothing
else that does. The absolute scale is therefore free for independent
measurement.

`extract.gdb` writes two files so that the two factors can be separated:

```
normdt.f32     = norm × dead time
norm_only.f32  = norm alone (the ApplyDeadtime step omitted)
dead time      = normdt.f32 / norm_only.f32
```

### Dead time is count-rate dependent and must not be compared with a constant

The dead-time kernel is

```
livetime = 1 / max((1−S·k1)(1−S·k2)(1−S·A)(1−S·B), 1/clip)
```

which is a function of the singles rate `S` and therefore cannot equal one
constant across cases. `PARAMS.md` section 1 does derive a *static* 3D dead-time
scalar from `sysGeometry` —
`(dt_3dint + dt_3dmux + dt_3dtiming) / dt_3dint = (1.85 + 0.0 + 0.20) / 1.85 =
1.10811` — but comparing `normdt/norm_only` against that value is wrong in
principle, not merely wrong numerically.

> **Correction, 2026-09-08.** Two statements about this formula, here and in
> `PARAMS.md` section 1, have since been shown to be wrong; see the erratum at
> the head of `PARAMS.md`. First, `k₁` and `k₂` are not
> `normDeadtimeSlopeInnerRing` and `normDeadtimeSlopeOuterRing` (4.74 and 4.57):
> the kernel reads `m_pDeadtimeStruct+0x78` = `intCorrFactor3d` (1.85) and
> `+0x80` = `timingCorrFactor3d` (0.20), while `+0x7c` = `muxCorrFactor3d` (0.0)
> is passed but unused. The pair 4.74 and 4.57 goes to
> `sharcApNormDeadtimeFactors` at 0x4ed860, called from `CAL2d::CreateTaskList`,
> which is the 2D calibration branch and a different computation. Second, the
> scalar `(a+b+c)/a` is not a configuration constant at all: `a`, `b` and `c`
> are `exSorterInputCoincCount`, `exSorterOverrunLosses` and
> `exCoincProcessorLosses`, three doubles that `rdfReadDeadTime` fills from the
> RDF header of the exam itself, so 1.1081 is not a value the kernel computes.
> Finally, `A` and `B` are two different arrays — `dt_3dpileUp_factors` along
> the ring axis, and the 6 × 9 table `dt_3dcrystalpileUp_factors` — rather than
> one table read twice.

Measured over all 60,679,584 bins, in two cases:

| case | singles | livetime | 1/livetime |
|---|---|---|---|
| NEMA bed 2 | 1.88 Mcps | 0.9874 | 1.0128 |
| paediatric bed 4 | 11.76 Mcps | 0.9339 | 1.0708 |

Livetime falls as singles rise, which is how dead time must behave, and that is
the usable evidence: it shows `normdt` is a *sensitivity* rather than a
correction factor. Dividing the data by it is what corrects.

A further cross-check: `out/dt_mux.f32` is entirely zero, consistent with
`dt_3dmuxCorrectionConstant = 0.0`.

### The dead-time arrays are per block, not per crystal

`m_pIntDeadtime` and `m_pMuxDeadtime` have length `blocksPerSystem` = 256
(64 blocksPerRing × 4), not 576 × 24. Reading past that length yields values of
the order of 7.9e34, which is the only indication that the end has been passed.
`extract.gdb` reads `blocksPerSystem` from the live parameter structure rather
than hard-coding it.

### `CNorm3d` and `CDeadtime3d` are built by writing fields, not by calling the constructor

Both constructors are plain assignments:

```
CNorm3d     (32 B): [0]=CRawDataMem*  [8]=paramStruct*  [0x10]=0 [0x18]=0
CDeadtime3d (56 B): [0]=CRawDataMem*  [8]=paramStruct*  [0x10..0x28]=0
                    [0x30]=1.0f
```

`extract.gdb` therefore writes the bytes directly. Calling the constructor
through a cast function pointer is refused by gdb, and the refusal is reported
as an ordinary command error, leaving the object as uninitialised `malloc`
memory until `Initialize()` fails somewhere entirely different.

---

## 3c. Randoms and scatter

`CIgManager::InitRandomsFromSingles()` does not produce a sinogram. It calls
`CalculateRFS()`, which calls `GE_meanvx` and `initRFSParams`, computing only
the randoms-from-singles *parameters*. That is why it returns
`GRE_IG_SUCCESS` while `m_pRandoms` remains entirely zero.

3D randoms are actually written in `COsem3dPrep::DoPrep(view, ...)`:

```
GetRawPromptsBuff / GetDelaysBuff / GetCorrPromptsBuff
Preprocess(...)                          -> sharcApPreprocess
SetCorrPromptsBuffValid
GetCorrRandomsBuff(view) -> Preprocess -> SetCorrRandomsBuffValid   <- RANDOMS
GetCorrNormDTBuff(view)  -> GE_vfill  -> ApplyNormalization/ApplyDeadtime
GetCorrScatterPromptsBuff(view) -> Preprocess
```

The line `GetCorrNormDTBuff → GE_vfill → ApplyNormalization → ApplyDeadtime` is
independent confirmation that the formula in section 3b is indeed the vendor's.

All three contexts construct successfully (`probes/prep.gdb`), with entry points
taken from the vtable:

```
CCTAC_3D              Init 0x43eef0  TaskList 0x441550  DoTask 0x441030
CScatterFully3dModel  Init 0x489a30  TaskList 0x48bba0  DoTask 0x48b5d0
COsem3dPrep           Init 0x482290  TaskList 0x434de0  DoTask 0x435e70
```

`probes/prep2.gdb` runs `COsem3dPrep::DoTask`, and the scatter model completes
every phase — `MSCAT_CONVERT_SCAT_TO_3D`, `MSCAT_TAILFIT_SCAT_3D`,
`MSCAT_TAILSCALE_SCAT_3D` — followed by
`CorrPrompts/CorrRandoms/CorrScatterPrompts::InsertedNewViews 0..48`.

The obstruction is attenuation rather than randoms or scatter. `DoPrep` loops at

```
CCTAC_3D:: AreViewsAvailable not ready Start: 0 Num: 47
```

because `CCTAC_3D` is a separate context. On the console the thread pool runs it
concurrently; here, with one thread, it must complete first. Running it first
makes `CCTAC_3D::DoTask` segfault at CTAC3D.cpp:320, because the CTAC image set
was never loaded — a different path from the PIFA that
`sharcCmpOpenDataFiles` reads.

Attenuation is not among the four quantities required, so `probes/prep4.gdb`
sets `IgJobReq.attenuationFlag = 0` and `fCTACFlag = 0` so that `DoPrep` skips
the CTAC branch. `DoPrep` then runs view by view — `Prep3d uiPhiIndex = N
Processing Done` — but stops at view 28 of 288: `/proc` shows utime static and
all eight threads asleep.

### Randoms and scatter are a pre-estimate, outside the OSEM loop

Prep does not wait for OSEM to consume a buffer. Reconstructing
`Do3dEmissionImage` in *source-line* order rather than address order makes this
clear:

```
IgManager.cpp:231   construct COsem3dPrep / CPrep3d
             247    CCorrDataMem::InvalidateBuffs
             248    CThreadPool::StartContext      <- prep released asynchronously
            1838    CCTAC_3D(ig)
            1911    CThreadPool::WaitContext       <- barrier
            1915    CThreadPool::WaitContext       <- barrier
            1944    CScatterFully3dModel(ig, n, bool)
            1948    WriteCorrDataByBrp
            1962    CThreadPool::WaitContext       <- barrier
            1994    CreateReconContext()           <- builds OSEM; internally calls
                                                      CombineAdditiveCorrBuffers
            2005    CThreadPool::RunContext        <- OSEM runs here (blocking)
            2039    Do3dOverlapProcessing
```

All three `WaitContext` calls complete before `CreateReconContext` at line 1994
and before OSEM's `RunContext` at line 2005. `CreateReconContext` is precisely
where `CombineAdditiveCorrBuffers()` is called, combining randoms and scatter
into the additive term.

Randoms and scatter are therefore estimated once, completely, before OSEM
begins. Within the OSEM loop there is only re-reading:
`OsemTof::COsemTofMain::GetRandomsViewData(view, float*)` copies from the
existing buffer and computes nothing.

`IgJobReq.modelScatterIterations` is an *internal* SSS loop that refines the
tail fit, not an OSEM loop.

The stall at view 28 therefore cannot be a wait on OSEM, which has not yet been
constructed. The cause is `CRendezvous(int)` together with
`CRendezvous::Join()`, a thread-counting barrier, used by
`CScatterFully3dModel::SyncBeforeNextIter`. Constructing the context with
`nThreads = 6`, the value `GetNumOfProcessingThreads` reports, and then running
`DoTask` on only one thread leaves a barrier waiting for six arrivals that never
open — which matches the observed symptom exactly: 0 % CPU and every thread
asleep.

### Setting `nThreads = 1` resolves it, and randoms complete over all 288 views

```
COsem3dPrep(ig, 1, ctac, scat)          CScatterFully3dModel(ig, 1, false)
-> 28 views  =>  281 views printed, m_pRandoms->m_uiCounterElement = 288
```

`out/randoms.f32` is 288 × 553 × 381 with no zero entries, ranging 0.0352 to
0.2473.

Physical verification:

```
total prompts   2.143e7 counts
total randoms   4.698e6 counts      -> randoms/prompts = 21.9 %
view-to-view spread: randoms 2.0 %   against   prompts 5.7 %
```

Randoms are markedly smoother across views, which is the expected form of a
from-singles estimate rather than noise.

### Scatter is not a second context running alongside prep

Decoding the vtable offsets in `CPrep3d::DoTask` (address point
`_ZTV11COsem3dPrep+16`):

```
*0x20 DoTask            *0x30 Finalize       *0x80 DoPrep / GetScatterCounts
*0x88 AddViewsToCorr    *0x90 AreViewsAvailable
*0xa0 DoPostCTACPrep    *0xa8 DoPostScatterPrep   *0xb0 DoPostRandomsPrep
```

Combined with the source line numbers:

```
Prep3d.cpp:406  GetNextTask + AddViewsToCorr
           422  AreViewsAvailable
           462  *0x20  -> calls DoTask() of the SCATTER MODEL, within this function
           473  CRendezvous::Join()      <- barrier 1
           475  DoPostCTACPrep
           484  CRendezvous::Join()      <- barrier 2
           500  *0x20  -> scatter DoTask again
           509  CRendezvous::Join()      <- barrier 3
           515  Finalize
           519  DoPostScatterPrep
           527  CRendezvous::Join()      <- barrier 4
           540  DoPostRandomsPrep
```

Scatter is a *phase within* `CPrep3d::DoTask`, invoked directly through the
`CScatter*` pointer that the constructor stores unconditionally at `this+0x190`
(constructor+264).

What runs in parallel is N thread-pool threads executing that same `DoTask`,
meeting at the four `CRendezvous::Join()` calls. `CRendezvous` is constructed in
`CPrep3d`'s constructor with exactly `nThreads` (constructor+289). Hence:

* `nThreads = 6` with only one thread calling `DoTask` leaves the barrier
  waiting for six arrivals, which never open, stalling at view 28 with 0 % CPU.
* `nThreads = 1` opens the barrier on the first arrival, so all 288 views run
  and randoms are produced.

### What disables scatter is `attenuationFlag`, not `nThreads`

Comparing `prep2` with `prep6`, the variable that actually differs between the
runs is `attenuationFlag`:

| run | attenuationFlag | nThreads | `MSCAT_` lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prep2` | 2 (enabled) | 6 | 97 |
| `prep4` | 0 (disabled) | 6 | 0 |
| `prep6` | 0 (disabled) | 1 | 0 |

Disabling attenuation to avoid the `CCTAC_3D` crash also disables SSS scatter,
which is physically reasonable, since SSS requires mu information.

The scatter problem is therefore: scatter requires `attenuationFlag` enabled;
enabling it requires `CCTAC_3D` to produce 47 attenuation views; and
`CCTAC_3D::Initialize` fails with
`ValidateCTAC radialModulesPerSystem EX: 32 CTAC: 0`, because the CTAC-side
`sysGeometry` structure is entirely zero, no CTAC file having ever been loaded.

Copying the full 2048 bytes of `sysGeometry` into `TransSysGeometry` passes
`ValidateCTAC` (section 3d). That is still not sufficient: `CCTAC_3D` is starved
of *input*, as measured:

```
$rd->m_pAttn   counter=0  alloc=47  elementSize=65536   <- 128*128*4, one mu slice
fileStatus[1] = 0        <- only the PIFA HEADER was parsed; no voxels were loaded
```

Loading 47 mu slices directly into `m_pAttn`, then calling `InsertedNewViews`
and `SetViewsAsValid`, reduces the number of `AreViewsAvailable not ready` polls
from 387 to 0.

### The working configuration: four conditions that must hold simultaneously

```
1. attenuationFlag ENABLED (left at 2, as the job has it)  <- disabling loses scatter
2. TransSysGeometry := sysGeometry (2048 bytes)            <- passes ValidateCTAC
3. mu-map loaded into CRawDataMem::m_pAttn (47 views × 128×128 f32, mm^-1)
                   + InsertedNewViews(0,47) + SetViewsAsValid(0,47)
4. nThreads = 1 when constructing CScatterFully3dModel and COsem3dPrep
```

The result is 288 of 288 views, 0 polls, and `m_pScatter` counter = 288.

```
radial roughness:  scatter 0.071  against  prompts 1.317  -> ~19× smoother
```

A scatter sinogram must be smooth and low-frequency; that roughness ratio is its
signature, and is the evidence that this is a genuine estimate rather than noise
or a copy of the data.

`DoTask` still terminates with SIGSEGV in
`CScatterFully3dModel::GetScatterCounts` (ScatterFully3dModel.cpp:5025), but
only *after* all 288 views have been written, so the result is unaffected.

The mu-map loading point in condition 3 is where a locally computed mu is
supplied; see section 3d and `ct_to_pifa.py`.

### A fifth condition, added 2026-08-27: whether scatter is TOF-resolved

```
5. IgJobReq.reconMethod = 3   ->  CScatterFully3dModel(ig, nThreads, TRUE)
                              ->  m_bTOFDim = 1  (offset 0x2d8)
                              ->  scatter_tof.f32 from CCorrDataMem::m_pScatterTOF
```

The constructor's third parameter is the TOF flag, and
`CIgManager::Do3dEmissionImage` computes it as exactly `(reconMethod == 3)`
(`0x42a6fc`: `cmpl $0x3 … ; sete %cl`). Setting it to 0 makes `CreateTaskList`
omit all five `MSCAT_*_TOF` tasks, and `m_pScatterTOF` — still allocated at
288 × 151360 B on every run — remains empty.

Measured on paediatric bed 1, enabled against disabled: `randoms.f32` is
bit-identical and `scatter.f32` differs by 0.04 % in total. Enabling it is
therefore a strict superset rather than a trade-off. `extract.gdb` enables it by
default; `D710_TOF=0` (or `estimate.py --no-tof`) disables it.

## 3d. Supplying a locally computed mu-map to the vendor pipeline

This answers the SSS question: it is possible, and it does not require the
console.

The PIFA file *is* the mu-map container that the scatter model reads.
`sharcCmpOpenDataFiles` parses it into the global `transmissionCTACHeader`, and
`CScatterFully3dModel` builds the mu image from it. The job points at it through
exactly one field:

```
IgJobReq.inputTransmissionFileName[0]      <- job.gdb line 12
```

### Format: every field, with names and offsets taken from DWARF

`ptype /o transmissionCTACHeader`; the global is `[3]`, one per acquisition:

```
  0  f32 versionID          (1.0)      32  s8  frame_of_reference[64]
  4  n32 cmpJobID                      96  s8  spareFields[64]
  8  n16 xMatrix            (128)     160  n32 offsetToStartOfImage = 164
 10  n16 yMatrix            (128)     --- end of the 164-byte header; then the
 12  n16 zMatrix            (47)          image block: xMatrix*yMatrix*zMatrix
 16  f32 ctacDfov           (700 mm)      float32, mu in mm^-1, x fastest
 20  n32 patientEntry
 24  n32 patientPosition
 28  f32 tableLocation      (−47.92)
```

Verified against the self-test file itself: 164 + 128×128×47×4 = 3,080,356
bytes, exactly the file size. The unit is mm⁻¹ rather than cm⁻¹: the measured
maximum is 0.009336 mm⁻¹ = 0.0934 cm⁻¹, consistent with water at 511 keV
(about 0.096 cm⁻¹). STIR uses cm⁻¹, so divide by ten.

### The dimension order of the mu block is established, not assumed

The question of whether the PIFA has the correct dimension order as well as the
correct total is answered by how the binary *consumes* the block.

`CRawDataMem::m_pAttn`, the buffer `CCTAC_3D` reads into, is allocated as:

```
$rd->m_pAttn   alloc = 47 views     = zMatrix
               elementSize = 65536  = 128 × 128 × 4 = xMatrix × yMatrix × f32
```

One view is therefore one z slice, and the layout must be

```
mu[z][y][x]   z slowest  ->  y  ->  x fastest
```

This is a structural constraint rather than a chosen convention: any other
layout gives a view size that does not match, and `CCTAC_3D` reads incorrectly
from the first slice onwards. `ct_to_pifa.py` writes exactly this order.

### `reorderDims*`: GE permutes internally, and it is not about patient orientation

The binary contains a family of three-dimensional permutation functions:

```
reorderDims132  reorderDims213  reorderDims231  reorderDims312  reorderDims321
        (int n1, int n2, int n3, float* in, float* out)
```

Decoding `reorderDims312` from the assembly:

```
in  :  idx = i1 + n1·i2 + n1·n2·i3      (i1 fastest)
out :  idx = i3 + n3·i1 + n3·n1·i2      (i3 fastest, then i1, then i2)
```

The name `reorderDimsABC` therefore denotes the axis order of the *output*,
fastest first, as A, B, C.

`CCTAC_3D::DoTask` calls either `ReorderDims312` or `ReorderDims132`, selected
by a seven-way jump table (`jmp *0xb4f668(,%rax,8)`, bounded by `cmp $0x6`).
That index is not a patient-orientation flag; it is `CTAC_TASK_TYPE::taskType`,
that is, the pipeline stage:

```
struct CTAC_TASK_TYPE { CTAC_TASK taskType; uint uiInputStartView; ... }
```

and GE's own log prints `CCTAC_3D:: CTAC task 6 Input: 0 47 Output: 0 47`, so
task 6 selects branch 6 and `ReorderDims312`. This is an internal transposition
between phases, from the CT block into the order the forward projector expects,
and it occurs regardless of how the PIFA is written. It does not read
`patientEntry` or `patientPosition`.

### Sign conventions, measured using GE's own table-masking code

`reorderDims*` are pure transpositions without sign inversion, so they say
nothing about whether row 0 is anterior or posterior. The scatter module does.

`CScatterFully3dModel::MaskTableMuImage` calls `sharcApTableMaskModified`, which
models the patient table as a fixed circle:

```
constants in the binary:  r = 464.05 mm      offset = 45.974
position taken from:  paramStruct+0x8c18 / +0x8c1c
                = ctacXaxisTranslation / ctacYaxisTranslation
                (XOR with −0.0, that is, negated)
then:  rotate(mu, out, 128, 128, sysGeometry.vqc_ZaxisRoll)
```

GE therefore knows where the table lies within the mu block and removes it. That
is what distinguishes the sign: if y is flipped, the mask cuts into tissue, the
table remains in the mu-map as dense material, and SSS inflates scatter.

Measured on the same NEMA bed 2, varying only the orientation of the mu block:

| mu-map | scatter sum | S/(T+S) | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| LPS as written | 4.037e6 | 32.98 % | 0.673 |
| y flipped | 6.031e6 | 49.28 % | 0.924 |
| x flipped | 4.133e6 | 33.77 % | 0.683 |

The y axis is thereby established: 32.98 % lies within the physical range for 3D
PET (30–45 %), whereas 49.28 % does not. LPS as written is correct.
`ct_to_pifa.py` writes in DICOM patient coordinates, taking `x0` and `y0`
directly from `ImagePositionPatient`, which is what GE expects.

On NEMA the x axis cannot be resolved (33.77 against 32.98, a 2.4 % relative
difference, both plausible), because the phantom is nearly symmetric about x and
an x flip is therefore almost invisible. The table is offset in y, so only y is
strongly constrained.

### The x axis, established on a real patient case

The same measurement was repeated on a chest-abdomen bed of a patient
(`11082026`, `SINO0004`, table at −270.68 mm, 43.8 M prompts), chosen because
its mu-map is 22.1 % left-right asymmetric, which is what NEMA lacks:

| mu-map | S/(T+S) | tail residual L–R difference |
|---|---|---|
| LPS as written | 37.28 % | 83.8 % |
| x flipped | 76.48 % | 105.3 % |

76 % is not physically possible, since scatter cannot constitute 76 % of trues.
LPS as written is therefore correct on the x axis as well. The patient case
discriminates far more strongly than NEMA (37 against 76, compared with 33.0
against 33.8), exactly as the asymmetry predicts.

> One figure in this check is easily misread: `prompts − randoms − scatter` is
> negative at 54.7 % of bins. That does not indicate a wrong model — 54 % of
> bins hold zero counts (the median is 0, and 94 % of bins hold at most 2
> counts), so `0 − randoms − scatter` is negative by construction. Filtering by
> count:
>
> ```
> bins with prompts > 0  (46.0 % of bins):  1.5 % negative
> bins with prompts > 2  ( 5.9 % of bins):  0.0 % negative
> ```
>
> And in total, `randoms + scatter` is 71.9 % of prompts, leaving 28 % trues,
> which is reasonable.

Both axes have therefore been measured, and DICOM LPS as written is correct.
`ct_to_pifa.py` accordingly has no flip flag: both flips change the result
strongly, so they are something to be re-measured rather than toggled
experimentally. A different machine or export with another convention should
repeat the measurement above.

This is consistent with a geometric check on the mu-map itself:

```
central slice: y centroid 67.5 (array centre 64)
total mu, half y<64 (anterior) 7.8   half y>=64 (posterior) 12.5
-> the denser half is at HIGH y, so the couch lies BELOW the phantom, as LPS requires
```

> A direct comparison with a genuine vendor PIFA is not possible:
> `/usr/g/ctuser/PIFA/<exam>/` appears in the console log but is not in the
> export, so there is no reference file. The table-mask measurement substitutes
> for it, and is stronger than an appeal to visual plausibility.

### Tools

```bash
python3 make_pifa.py --inspect <file>.dat
python3 make_pifa.py mu.npy my.pifa --dfov 700 --units cm-1 \
        --copy-spare-from <sample_pifa>.dat
```

then point line 12 of `job.gdb` at `my.pifa`.

`make_pifa.py` has been verified by round trip: rewriting from the payload of
the self-test file produces a byte-identical file.

One uncertainty remains. `spareFields[64]` (offsets 96 to 159) is not empty in
GE's file; it holds `2.5`, `6`, `3`, `64.0` and several small floats. DWARF
names the field "spare", so `pet_recon`'s parser has no name with which to read
it — but that is an inference rather than a measurement. `--copy-spare-from`
copies those 64 bytes verbatim from a PIFA known to work, so that the question
need not be decided.

### `ValidateCTAC` checks about twenty fields, not four

The overload the real `pet_recon` calls is 0x43e550,
`ValidateCTAC(jobReq, apConfig, petExam, acqParam×2, sorter×2, sysGeo×2)`, and
it compares field by field, each with its own error message:

```
radial/axialModulesPerSystem   radial/axialBlocksPerModule
radial/axialCrystalsPerBlock   detectorRadialSize   detectorAxialSize
effectiveRingDiameter          transaxial_crystal_0_offset
vqc_XaxisTranslation  vqc_YaxisTranslation  vqc_ZaxisRoll
scanner_first_slice   interCrystalPitch   interBlockPitch     <- SYS_GEO
patientEntry   patientPosition   tableLocation                <- PIFA header
```

There is a smaller overload at 0x43e400 comparing only four fields, which the
real reconstruction does not call. Twenty fields are nevertheless easier rather
than harder: every geometric field compares `sysGeometry` (EX) against
`TransSysGeometry` (CTAC), so copying 2048 bytes from one to the other makes
every comparison an identity (section 3c). The remaining three fields are in the
PIFA header and are written by `make_pifa.py` and `ct_to_pifa.py`.

`frame_of_reference` must match the exam. The comparison is a `strcmp`, a
mismatch is rejected outright, and scatter then comes out entirely zero:

```
ValidateCTAC frame_of_reference EX: PIFA CTAC: 1.2.840.113619.2.290.3.663120...
```

A literal such as the string "PIFA" is rejected immediately. `ct_to_pifa.py`
defaults to the `FrameOfReferenceUID` of the CT series itself, which was
measured to match the value the vendor requires exactly.

### PIFA and CTAC are two entirely separate paths

| | read from | used for | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| PIFA | `inputTransmissionFileName[0]` | the scatter model (SSS) | working |
| CTAC | the CTAC image set, on a different path | the attenuation sinogram (`CCTAC_3D`) | SIGSEGV, never loaded |

The scatter model completes every phase (`MSCAT_CONVERT_SCAT_TO_3D`,
`MSCAT_TAILFIT_SCAT_3D`, `MSCAT_TAILSCALE_SCAT_3D`) *while* `CCTAC_3D` is
failing, which is direct evidence that SSS requires only the PIFA. Setting
`attenuationFlag = 0` when scatter is wanted is therefore wrong rather than an
omission.

### `PARAMS.md`: the live parameters

Not a sinogram, but what is needed in order to implement the formulae: the whole
of `apCfg` and `sysGeometry` read from the running process, with full field
names from DWARF. Of the three points it was originally said to settle, only the
third still stands:

* `delaysCorrectionFactor = 1.0`, so GE applies no additional factor to randoms.

The other two — the static dead-time scalar of 1.1081, and the identification of
`A[i]` and `B[j]` with a single `dt_3dcrystalpileUp_factors` table — were
corrected on 2026-09-08 and are superseded by the erratum at the head of
`PARAMS.md`, summarised in the correction note in section 3b above.

See `PARAMS.md` for the detail and for two useful negative results.

### The measurements are self-verifying

`sharcCmpOpenDataFiles` returns 0 and fills `apCfg` with exactly the values that
static reading of the configuration files and the binary had already implied:

| `apCfg` field | live value | static reading |
|---|---|---|
| `normDeadtimeSlopeInnerRing` | 4.74 | 4.74 (the 2D calibration branch; see the correction in section 3b) |
| `normDeadtimeSlopeOuterRing` | 4.57 | 4.57 (likewise) |
| `scatScaleFactorLimit` | 1.5 | `SCAT_SCALE_FACTORS_LIMIT` |
| `norm3dGeometryPeriod` | 9 | 9, so the block is 3429 = 381 × 9 |
| `norm3dCorrXtalEffClipValue` | 10.0 | the dead-time `clip` |
| `scatCountRateFuncCoeff[11]` | 0.4509, 0.0709, 0.0193, −0.2785, … | 11 count-rate coefficients |

The printed RDF header agrees as well: `coincTimingPrecision 0.089246` ns is the
89.2459 ps used in `2τ = 55 × 89.2459 ps`; `delayedEvents 0`, `singleCollect 1`;
and segment type 9 at offset 118784 is the geometry-coefficient block of the
norm file described in `cal/README.md`.

Those values are confirmed by the binary at run time rather than by reading the
configuration files.

### The job path through `sharcCmpProcessJobOnAp` is unusable

`sharcCmpProcessJobOnAp` returns −1 immediately at cpcApLib.cpp:412, at
`write(fdCpcIgFIFO, {2,0}, 8)`. That FIFO is opened by `CPCCommThread`, which is
terminated at boot. Substituting a `pipe()` gets past the `write()` and then
deadlocks: `/proc` shows the main thread in `poll_schedule_timeout`, six workers
in `futex_do_wait`, zero CPU seconds and 15 MB RSS. The reason is architectural:
`ProcessJobOnAp` is the host/CPC side, which dispatches work to the IG side and
waits, but gdb calls it from the main thread already inside
`CIgManager::RunCyclic`, that is, from the IG side. The only thread that could
answer is the thread that is waiting.

Section 3a replaces this path entirely by calling the functions `RunCyclic`
calls directly, with no job layer, no FIFO and no handshake.
`run_job.gdb` and `run_job_fifo.gdb` are kept as evidence for this conclusion
and should not be run.

### Going further: calling the kernels directly

The four corrections are four thin wrappers:

```
CNorm3d::ApplyNormalization(float* inBuff, int phi, float* pWorkBuffer, bool)
                                                      -> sharcAp3dNormalization
CDeadtime3d::ApplyDeadtime(float* inBuff, int phi, float* outBuff, int countsFlag,
                           float* totalCounts, float* averageDeadtimeFactor,
                           float* pDeadtimeWorkBuff, bool)
                                                      -> sharcApDeadtime3d_puc
sharcApPreprocess                                     <- randoms, through CPrep3d
CScatterFully3dModel::*                               -> calcScatter3d
```

The parameter names above are the real DWARF names, which gdb prints at a
faulting frame. The first two wrappers only extract scalars and pointers from
`m_pRawDataMem`, `m_pIgParams` and the two globals `apCfg` and `sysGeometry`,
all four of which section 3a populates correctly. `extract.gdb` calls these two
functions directly.

---

## 4. Known pitfalls

### gdb

* **The direction flag leaks into inferior calls.** gdb builds the dummy frame
  from the register state at the stop point, including EFLAGS. Whatever DF holds
  in `pet_recon` when it stopped is what the called function starts with. With
  DF = 1, the `rep stos` of glibc's `memset` runs backwards:
  `CCyclicMemBuffer::AllocateMem` (CyclicMemBuffer.cpp:160), while clearing a
  freshly allocated 121 MB buffer, runs off the *front* of the buffer and
  segfaults after 13 bytes, with `rdi = m_pStartBuffer − 17` and `si_addr` on
  the page below. The System V ABI guarantees DF = 0 at every call boundary, so
  the compiler never emits `cld`, and nothing in the inferior restores it.
  The symptom is misleading: it *appears* random, because DF depends on where
  the process happened to stop, and is easily mistaken for flakiness while being
  entirely deterministic. The remedy is
  `set $eflags = $eflags & ~0x400` before each call (`clear_df()` in `lib.gdb`,
  and once in `boot.gdb`).
* **gdb refuses to `print` a function returning `void`, and reports it as an
  ordinary command error.** Casting to `((void (*)(...)) addr)(...)` and then
  printing means the constructor never runs, the object remains uninitialised
  `malloc` memory, and `Initialize()` fails somewhere entirely different. Cast
  to `(int (*)(...))` and discard the return value, or — better for a
  constructor that only assigns — write the fields directly.
* **A wrapper must not swallow gdb's error messages.** The first version printed
  `<unavailable>` for every failure, making a syntax rejection look identical to
  a crash in the callee. `lib.gdb` prints the error verbatim.
* **`set scheduler-locking on` must come after `run`.** Before that there are no
  threads, gdb reports `Target 'exec' cannot support this command` and aborts
  the entire script file. It belongs at the end of `boot.gdb`.
  Locking by default is correct: every inferior call resumes *all* threads,
  which would let six processing threads race the allocator. Unlock
  (`unlocked()` in `lib.gdb`) only for calls that genuinely need the thread
  pool, which are `LoadRawData` and the loading functions.
* **`sharcCmpDebugFlag = 0x1FF` prints about 50,000 lines of RDF header** through
  a pipe and accounts for most of a run's duration. Use `0x4` (LOAD) for normal
  work, and `0x1FF` only when a header dump is needed, which is the source of
  `PARAMS.md`.
* **gdb buffers its own stdout while the inferior's `printf` does not**, so logs
  interleave out of order and a run that hangs leaves no record of how far it
  reached. `lib.gdb` flushes after every line, in `say()`.
* **Do not place `petsw/usr/lib64` on gdb's own `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.** gdb picks up
  GE's ancient `libstdc++.so.6` and fails to start. Symlink only the five
  required libraries into a separate directory, and set the variable for the
  *inferior* with `set environment` inside gdb.
* **Do not call `strcpy` in the inferior to load a string.** It encounters
  glibc's ifunc resolution, and every inferior function call resumes all
  threads, which is enough for the comm thread to reach `exit()` and kill the
  process. Write memory directly with
  `gdb.selected_inferior().write_memory` (the `_s` function in `boot.gdb`).
* **`/petRDFS/OVLFILES` cannot be created inside the namespace**, since `/`
  belongs to the real root. It is not needed: the overlap path is in the `.job`
  itself, and `job2gdb.py` accepts a directory argument to override it.
* **`ptype S_HOST_CMP_JOB_REQ` is unavailable**, the structure being anonymous in
  DWARF. Use the global `IgJobReq` (cpcMain.cpp:108) and cast function pointers
  at the call site.

### Process and container

* **Only one `pet_recon` may run at a time, and a hung instance blocks every
  other.** `cupInit.c:186` prints `pet_recon already running @ pid=NNN,
  exiting...` and exits with status 1. gdb has done nothing at that point, so
  the failure appears in an obscure form (`Cannot access memory at address
  0xf389a4`, which is a read of `sharcCmpDebugFlag` in a process that has
  already exited). An interrupted run leaves an orphan process idle at 15 MB RSS
  and 0 % CPU, which is easily mistaken in `ps` for nothing at all. Check and
  clear before each run:

  ```bash
  pkill -9 -f pet_recon
  ```

  gdb cannot attach to it (`ptrace: Inappropriate ioctl`) because it is in its
  own namespace, so it can only be killed. Under docker, use `docker ps` and
  then `docker rm -f`.
* **`ps` inside an agent sandbox does not see processes in the namespace.**
  `ps aux | grep pet_recon` returns nothing while `/proc/<pid>/comm` still reads
  `pet_recon`. Do not trust `ps`; check `/proc` instead:

  ```bash
  for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do [ "$(cat $p/comm 2>/dev/null)" = pet_recon ] && echo $p; done
  ```
* **Distinguish computation from deadlock using `utime` and `stime` in
  `/proc/<pid>/stat`** rather than by elapsed time. `utime=0 stime=0` with 15 MB
  RSS means nothing has been done. `wchan` indicates where it is waiting.
* **`/etc/hosts` cannot be baked into the image.** `RUN ... >> /etc/hosts` in the
  Dockerfile fails with exit status 2, because the daemon bind-mounts that file
  at run time. Use `--add-host`, which `run.sh` already does. Without it the
  process dies in `gethostbyname` before anything else is attempted.
* **`/usr/PET/systemConfig` must be writable.** The configuration manager opens
  `local/cmcfg.xml` read-write; mounting it `:ro` fails at start-up with
  `ConfigManager():Error on trying to open XML file`, then
  `InitializeCM():Error in Object creation`, then exit 255. `d710:full` leaves
  it writable in the image layer.
* **gdb cannot call an inlined function**: `Cannot evaluate function -- may be
  inlined`, encountered with `CRawDataMem::GetPromptsBuff`. Read the field
  directly, taking the offset from `ptype /o`.

---

## 5. Why a `.job` maps directly onto `IgJobReq`

`IgJobReq` is a static variable at cpcMain.cpp:108, and its field names match
the `#...` labels in the `.job` file character for character:
`emissionScatterFlag`, `emissionRandomsFlag`, `normalizationFlag`,
`emissionDeadTimeFlag`, `hrActivityFactor`, `scatter3dPatientCutoff`,
`modelScatterMultiplesNorm` and the rest. `job2gdb.py` matches on the label, so
an ordering discrepancy raises an error rather than silently writing the wrong
field.

The final group (`cmpProcessingPacketID`, `sliceNumber`,
`fileRead3dOverlap`/`fileWrite3dOverlap`, `cmpPacketDataType`,
`wellCounterValue`) belongs to the sub-structure `cmpPackets[100]`. The `.job`
file lists these flat, repeating one group per packet, so `job2gdb.py`
re-indexes each time it encounters `cmpProcessingPacketID`. The sample XR job
has 47 packets, matching `numberOfProcessingPackets = 47`.
